# JM Lathe Corpus Profile — "how we programmed it" + optimization gaps (data-grounded)

**Owner:** kilo · **Date:** 2026-06-01 · **Unit:** U-CAM-CORPUS-PROFILE
**/goal clause:** *"go over how all previous CAD/CAM programs were written, take notes on how we generated them (we were inefficient), learn to optimize."* This is the empirical, real-data answer — generated by `mcp-server/scripts/cam-corpus-profile.mts` running the (fixed) `CAMFeatureExtractorEngine` over a strided JM `CNC LATHE` sample.

## Empirical profile (77 parsed programs, strided sample)
| signal | observed |
|---|---|
| op-strategy totals | profile **71** · face **60** · drill **49** · thread **38** · bore **26** · other 12 · pocket 0 |
| spindle max rpm | min 600 · **median 800** · max 6000 (G50-capped CSS world; 6000 = live-tool/small-dia outlier) |
| feed-per-rev coverage | **7/77 (9.1%)** — only programs with an explicit G95 |
| feed mm/min coverage | 4/77 (5.2%) — only G94 or G95+G97-rpm |
| feed-per-rev values | 0.0015–3.0 in/rev, **median 0.005** (3.0 = a coarse thread lead) |
| feed-per-rev unit tag | **all 7 = "unknown"** (no G20/G21 declared); 70/77 = "none" (no feed-mode at all) |

## THE load-bearing finding (sharpens follow-up #43)
The U-CAM-FEED-PER-REV regex fix unlocked feed *parsing* (91→817 feed-lines, 9×), **but coverage is still ~9%** because **70 of 77 JM programs declare NEITHER a feed mode (G94/G95) NOR units (G20/G21)** — they rely entirely on the **Okuma machine power-on default**. The extractor (correctly, units-first) refuses to assume, so those 817 now-parseable feed values are captured-but-skipped rather than mislabeled.

→ **The dominant blocker to feed-model training is no longer the regex — it is the implicit-mode problem.** Resolving the JM Okuma OSP default feed mode (per-rev vs per-min) + default unit (inch per JM convention, but unconfirmed in-program) would unlock feed training across the whole corpus. This is a **units-first decision**, not an assumption I will make unilaterally (a wrong guess = the 25.4× / 10× IPR-vs-IPM error class). Tracked: **U-CAM-FEEDREV-MODE-DEFAULT (#43)**. Likely resolution: JM Okuma OSP lathes default to feed-per-rev (IPR) + inch — confirm via a machine parameter sheet or one operator/echo-post check, then re-profile.

## Per-family optimization gaps (the "learn to optimize" targets — from the 8-family analyses + this profile)
Time · efficiency · safety · accuracy. Cutting numbers stay physics-delegated (no inlined constants).
1. **OD roughing/finishing** — observed SFM ~250 (G96), spindle median 800 rpm: **conservative**. Modern carbide steel envelope is 600–1000+ SFM. Gap: speed. + redundant air-cut passes (3 G1 at same Z then a cycle — only pass 1 cuts). Optimize: physics-set SFM for {ISO,grade}; stock-aware Fusion roughing eliminates air passes.
2. **Threading** (38 ops) — fixed 0.003"/pass DOC across all pitches; constant 250–300 rpm → SFM swings 25–123. Optimize: decreasing-DOC infeed (constant chip area) + pitch/dia-aware rpm or G96.
3. **Grooving** — manual multi-pass (one file = 41 hand-coded G0/G1 blocks) instead of a peck-groove cycle. Optimize: Okuma **G74 peck-and-shift** (radial) or **G81/G82 LAP** (profile/face groove), 5–10× less code + no Z-offset typos. NOTE: NOT Fanuc G75 (corrected 2026-06-01 — G75 absent in the 16,558-program JM Okuma corpus).
4. **ID boring** (26 ops) — 50–75 SFM inferred (vs modern carbide 200+), feed 0.0015 (vs 0.003–0.005 possible), hardcoded G97. Optimize: raise within L/D deflection budget; G96 where dia varies.
5. **Drilling** (49 ops) — all G97 fixed rpm; 0.14" and 0.375" drills run near-identical rpm (wastes 10–25% on big drills). Optimize: per-dia rpm; dia-proportional peck.
6. **Parting** — defensive double-limit (G96 S250 + G50 S600 leaves margin); multi-pass air-cut rapids = 30–50% of a 0.2" cutoff cycle. Optimize: trim G50 to true safe-max; feed taper to center.
